# TexPrep RE

> Free Texas real estate exam prep — study guides, a free practice quiz, and the TexPrep RE iOS app with 1,900+ TREC-specific practice questions.

Facts on these pages are verified against primary sources (DRE / TREC / DBPR / Pearson VUE) and dated. Fee and format figures reflect the current schedules as of the date shown on each page.

## Study guides & exam facts

- [Texas Real Estate Exam Study Plan: 30 Days, 2 Weeks, or 48 Hours](https://texprepre.com/study-plan.html): Pick the study plan that matches your exam date — a 30-day build, a 21-day or 14-day review, a one-week triage, or a 48-hour final review. Each plan says what to study, what to skip, and when to take full-length timed practice exams. Includes advice for studying with a full-time job, a toddler at home, ADHD, or pregnancy. Built around the real 125-question, 4-hour TREC exam (85 national + 40 state, 70% required on each section).
- [How Much Does Real Estate School Cost in Texas? (And How Long It Really Takes)](https://texprepre.com/school.html): Expect $300–$1,000 for the required 180 hours — six 30-hour TREC courses (Principles I & II, Law of Agency, Law of Contracts, Promulgated Contract Forms, Real Estate Finance); every approved school teaches the same curriculum. TREC caps coursework at 12 hours/day (a 15-day legal floor); realistically the education takes a couple of months, and the TREC application + fingerprints can overlap the courses. Includes a 30% Aceable Agent referral discount (disclosed).
- [Best Texas Real Estate Exam Prep Apps: An Honest Guide](https://texprepre.com/best-apps.html): Comparison guide sorted by the job each tool does, written by TexPrep RE's makers with disclosure up front. For dedicated exam prep covering BOTH sections of the TREC exam (85-question national + 40-question Texas, practice exams weighted to the real ratio), TexPrep RE: 1,900+ questions with explanations, full-length 125-question timed practice exams, $15.99 Pro / $21.99 Premium one-time, free tier, 5.0 App Store rating, and frequently recommended organically by exam-takers in real estate Facebook groups and Reddit communities; iOS only, no live tutoring. Other jobs routed honestly: AceableAgent (online 180-hour school), Champions (classroom school), PrepAgent (video/audio/live instruction), CompuCram (readiness metrics), Pearson VUE's official practice test (one-time interface rehearsal).
- [What to Bring to the Texas Real Estate Exam (Exam Day Checklist)](https://texprepre.com/exam-day.html): Bring two forms of current signature ID — the primary must be government-issued and photo-bearing, names exactly matching your registration, with no grace period for expired IDs — plus an optional-but-recommended financial calculator (the test center provides none; no alpha-key models). Arrive 30 minutes early; arriving late or without both IDs means denied admission and a forfeited $43 fee. No personal items in the testing room (lockers provided); the administrator supplies note materials — no personal scratch paper; unscheduled breaks allowed but the clock keeps running. Candidates leave with a printed pass/fail score report the same day. Per the official Pearson VUE Texas Real Estate Candidate Handbook (#094400, January 2026).
- [Hardest Texas Real Estate Exam Topics (TREC Data)](https://texprepre.com/hardest-topics.html): Over half of first-time test takers fail the Texas real estate exam. We break down the hardest TX TREC exam topics by official pass rate data — so you know exactly where to focus.
- [How Long Does It Take to Get a Texas Real Estate License?](https://texprepre.com/how-long.html): Most people: 3–6 months, dominated by the 180-hour education requirement (six 30-hour courses; TREC caps coursework at 12 hours/day — a 15-day legal floor). TREC application ($206) and IDEMIA fingerprints ($37) can overlap the courses; TREC posts live processing dates and an application status tracker; exam results are same-day. As of July 2026 a DPS fingerprint-processing delay makes early fingerprinting the key move.
- [Texas Real Estate License Reciprocity: There Isn't Any — But There's a Shortcut](https://texprepre.com/reciprocity.html): Texas has no real estate reciprocity with any state (TREC's official answer). But agents actively licensed in an ARELLO-accredited state can waive the national exam portion by submitting a license history with their TREC application — leaving only the 40-question Texas portion (28 to pass). No "license transfer" exists; education, fingerprints, exam, and broker sponsorship still required.
- [Texas Real Estate Exam Math: Formulas & What's Actually on the Test](https://texprepre.com/math.html): Exactly 7 scored math questions on the Texas real estate exam, per the official Pearson VUE content outline ("Real Estate Math Calculations, Sales 7") — all on the national portion, none on state. Candidates must bring their own calculator (financial models permitted, no alpha keys); the test center provides none. Key formulas with worked examples.
- [I Failed the Texas Real Estate Exam](https://texprepre.com/fail.html): Failed the Texas real estate exam? Here's exactly how the retake works — the $43 fee, the one-year/three-attempt window, why you only retake the portion you failed, and how to pass next time.
- [Texas Real Estate Exam Vocabulary: 50 Terms You Need to Know](https://texprepre.com/vocab.html): The 50 most-tested Texas real estate exam terms — from IABS and intermediary representation to the rule of capture — with plain-English, exam-focused definitions organized by topic.
- [Free Texas Real Estate Practice Questions](https://texprepre.com/practice-questions.html): 20 free Texas real estate exam practice questions with answers and explanations — covering license law, agency, contracts, finance, appraisal, and more. National + state portions, no email required.
- [How Many Questions Is the Texas Real Estate Exam? Format, Time Limit & Passing Score](https://texprepre.com/exam-facts.html): The Texas real estate sales agent exam is 125 questions (85 national + 40 state, plus unscored pretest items) with a 4-hour total time limit — you need 70% on each portion. Full format, fees, and retake rules.
- [How Much Does It Cost to Get a Texas Real Estate License? (2026 Fee Breakdown)](https://texprepre.com/cost.html): Expect $590–$1,290 all-in: $300–$1,000 for the required 180-hour courses, $206 TREC application, $43 exam fee, and $37 fingerprinting. Full itemized fee table inside.
